_why: The SDK source tree uses uv-dynamic-versioning (pyproject.toml:5-6) and the read clone carries no git tags, so it cannot state its own version. `pydantic-ai-slim==2.35.0` in requirements.txt is a LABEL; these digests are the assertion. Review proved the distinction mattered THREE TIMES: with only the version pin, external.py could be edited and all 18 gates still passed; with the five-file pin of round 2, native_tools/__init__.py -- the module that decides which tools may be ADMITTED -- was unpinned and could be edited with all 26 gates still passing; with the sixteen-file pin of round 3, models/__init__.py was unpinned, so resolve_request_tools (models/__init__.py:1812-1930) -- the function that actually FILTERS native tools against supported_native_tools at :1849 -- could be neutered in a scratch SDK copy with `pin holds: 16 files` and all 47 gates still green. Round 5 made it FOUR times: with the nineteen-file pin, `tool_manager.py` -- where the tool body is actually invoked (`_raw_execute`, tool_manager.py:1008, `await self.toolset.call_tool(...)`) -- was unpinned, so wrapping that call in `except NotImplementedError:` in a scratch SDK copy turned ExternalToolset's fail-closed refusal fail-OPEN inside the pipeline while verify_pin.py still printed `pin holds: 19 files` and all 53 gates passed.
_algorithm: sha256 of the file bytes, as installed under site-packages/pydantic_ai/
_coverage: verify_pin.REQUIRED_PINS, plus test_gate.py's AST scan of every pydantic_ai module harness.py or test_gate.py imports from (ancestor package __init__.py files included since 2026-08-28). Regenerate deliberately with `python verify_pin.py --record`.
_coverage_frontier_why: ADDED 2026-08-28 (round 4). What is DELIBERATELY OUT of the pin, stated rather than left implicit. The pin covers the files whose bytes an assertion in this spike depends on directly. `_coverage_frontier` is the one-level transitive edge: every pydantic_ai module a PINNED file imports and that is not itself pinned, computed by verify_pin.frontier() and compared on every check. It is not pinned because the transitive closure at this SDK is effectively the whole distribution (284 modules, including every vendor model adapter -- models/anthropic.py, models/bedrock.py and so on -- reached only because models/__init__.py names them, and none of which any assertion here touches). Pinning them would make the gate red for edits that cannot affect the boundary. Recording them makes the boundary of the pin checkable: a pinned file that grows a new import into a module nobody has looked at fails check() until someone decides whether it belongs in REQUIRED_PINS. CORRECTED 2026-08-28 (round 5), superseding rather than erasing: the justification above -- "none of which any assertion here touches" -- was FALSE for three of the modules it covered. `tool_manager.py` is where `ExternalToolset.call_tool`'s unconditional NotImplementedError (toolsets/external.py:46, this spike's first cited claim) either propagates or does not; `capabilities/_tool_search.py` and `toolsets/_tool_search.py` decide that the agent runs a ToolSearchToolset WRAPPING the harness's ExternalToolset, which gate 13 now asserts. All three moved into REQUIRED_PINS and out of this frontier. The blanket phrase was the defect: the frontier is the set nobody has LOOKED at, and 'not looked at' was being written down as 'not depended on'.
